questions.question: A Python worker receives summarization jobs from an Azure Service Bus queue. A job must not be lost if the worker process stops unexpectedly while it is processing the message. Which approach should you use?

options.text: Receive in peek-lock mode and call complete_message after processing succeeds
options.why: Correct. The message stays in the queue while locked. If the worker stops, the lock expires and the message is delivered again.

options.text: Receive in receive-and-delete mode and process the message afterwards
options.why: Receive-and-delete removes the message on delivery, so a failure during processing loses it.

options.text: Call peek_messages and delete the message after processing
options.why: Peeking does not lock the message, so other receivers can process it at the same time, and peek is not a settlement operation.

options.text: Set the message time to live to zero
options.why: A very short time to live makes the message expire, which increases the chance of losing it.

questions.explanation: Peek-lock is the default receive mode. The message is removed only when the receiver completes it, which gives at-least-once processing.

questions.scenario: A function receives a message in peek-lock mode. A downstream model endpoint returns a temporary throttling error.
questions.question: You need the message to become available for another delivery attempt immediately. Which method should you call?

options.text: abandon_message
options.why: Correct. Abandon releases the lock so the message can be received again, and the delivery count increases.

options.text: complete_message
options.why: Complete removes the message from the queue, so the job would never be retried.

options.text: defer_message
options.why: Defer sets the message aside. It can then be received only by its sequence number, not by a normal receive.

options.text: renew_message_lock
options.why: Renewing the lock keeps the message hidden from other receivers for longer, which is the opposite of the requirement.

questions.explanation: Abandoning a message returns it to the queue. After the maximum delivery count is exceeded, it is moved to the dead-letter queue.

questions.question: You are creating an Azure Service Bus queue for order messages. Messages for the same customer must be processed in the order in which they were sent, while messages for different customers can be processed in parallel. What should you configure?

options.text: Enable sessions on the queue and set the session ID of each message to the customer ID
options.why: Correct. A session receiver locks all messages with the same session ID and processes them in order.

options.text: Enable duplicate detection on the queue
options.why: Duplicate detection drops repeated messages with the same message ID. It does not guarantee ordering per customer.

options.text: Increase the lock duration to five minutes
options.why: Lock duration controls how long a message is hidden. It does not group messages by customer.

options.text: Use the Basic tier with a single receiver
options.why: The Basic tier does not support sessions, and a single receiver removes the required parallelism across customers.

questions.explanation: Message sessions provide ordered, exclusive handling of related messages. Sessions must be enabled when the queue is created.

questions.question: A Python application must send messages to an Azure Service Bus queue by using Microsoft Entra ID authentication. No secrets can be stored in the application configuration. Which TWO actions should you perform?

options.text: Create the ServiceBusClient with the fully_qualified_namespace parameter and DefaultAzureCredential
options.why: Correct. This authenticates with Microsoft Entra ID instead of a connection string.

options.text: Assign the Azure Service Bus Data Sender role to the application's managed identity
options.why: Correct. The identity needs a data-plane role that allows sending to the queue.

options.text: Store the RootManageSharedAccessKey connection string in an environment variable
options.why: A connection string contains a shared access key, which is a secret.

options.text: Assign the Reader role on the namespace to the managed identity
options.why: Reader allows viewing the resource configuration only. It does not grant permission to send messages.

questions.explanation: Entra ID authentication requires a credential such as DefaultAzureCredential and a Service Bus data role assignment for the identity.

questions.question: A worker takes approximately three minutes to process each message from a queue that uses the default settings. The same message is often processed by two workers. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The message lock expires before processing completes, so the message is delivered to another worker
options.why: Correct. The default lock duration is one minute. After it expires, the message becomes visible again.

options.text: The maximum delivery count is set to 10
options.why: The maximum delivery count controls when a message is dead-lettered. It does not cause concurrent processing.

options.text: The queue uses the Standard tier
options.why: The Standard tier supports peek-lock in the same way as Premium, so the tier is not the cause.

options.text: Duplicate detection is disabled
options.why: Duplicate detection prevents duplicate sends. It does not prevent the same message being delivered again after a lock expires.

questions.explanation: Increase the lock duration (maximum five minutes) or renew the lock during processing, and make the handler idempotent.
